payload.rebuttal: argued: The task's own notes told me directly to leave this undriven: "A symlink is never a candidate... measured on the host's git 2.54.0... The cell image's git 2.39.5 is unmeasured. No witness drives a symlink as a reader." That is an explicit author instruction, not an omission I introduced. The same reliance on git grep's symlink exclusion already exists in this file's pre-existing retirement_markers function, so this is an established pattern, not a new risk. The failure mode is also overstated: if a symlink were ever listed by git grep, removed_name_readers still calls file_at on it, which either resolves it to its target's content for the normal word check or raises UnreadablePath/UnicodeDecodeError, which my code catches and keeps as a reader regardless. So a symlink that reaches my code is never silently dropped; the only real gap is whether git 2.39.5's grep emits it at all, which is exactly the unmeasured case the spec named and declined to test. Closing that gap needs a measurement on the cell's own git, which is a follow-up, not a change this spec asked for.
